statement: The maximum number of ordinary real circles tangent to three general real circles is eight, and this maximum is attained.

answer.text: The maximum number of ordinary real circles tangent to three general real circles is eight, and this maximum is attained.
answer.qualification: Generic ordinary-circle regime of Stoll’s classification; special or completed fibres are separate.

source.location: Unnumbered table and following argument, original p.626
source.version: Original German journal article (1873), GDZ article scan; PDF page 1 is a digitization cover, original p.613 begins on PDF page 2.

scope: Three ordinary real input circles with strictly ordered positive radii and general centres, excluding mutual tangencies and the collinear-centre/zero-radius/straight-line special loci discussed separately.
notes:
The finite maximum is not an upper bound on the size of exceptional infinite fibres in a completed problem.

Source discussion. The generic real maximum is 8; table cases 1, 6 and 10 attain it.
